## Natural history notes

A tiny metallic wood-boring beetle characterized by a compact, flattened, oval body and dark bronzy to metallic coloration typical of small Brachys jewel beetles. In Florida, Brachys floricola is recorded as part of the state’s buprestid fauna and is most likely encountered in warm wooded or shrubby habitats, forest edges, scrubby areas, and places with suitable broadleaf host plants. Adults may rest on foliage, while the larvae of Brachys species are leaf miners that feed concealed between the upper and lower leaf surfaces, creating blotch-like mines and linking plant foliage to predators and parasitoid wasps.
